To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) high-angular resolution polarized observations can be used to discriminate among different models of collapse; (2) the observations are consistent with models of magnetized collapse; (3) magnetic field dissipation, if it occurs, is below the resolution limit of the observations; (4) ALMA can distinguish among the models considered in this work.

1) the magnetic fields in the plane of NGC 1333 are aligned with the rotation of the protostellar disk; 2) the magnetic field is likely to be amplified in the collapsing core, but not to the level that it would prevent star formation; 3) the collapse is likely to be triggered by the presence of a magnetic field, but not by magnetic dissipation; and 4) the collapse is not likely to be triggered at the level of the cloud, but

the best fit to the polarized emission observed toward IRAS 2A is obtained for a model of collapse with mass-to-fluxe ratio of the order of 2, magnetic field strength of the order of ~0.5-1 mG, and a protostellar age of the order ~5 10^4 yrs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of low mass stars and the role of the magnetic fields in the star formation process.
the study of the physical processes occurring during the formation of low- and high-mass stars, and with the development of new theoretical and computational tools for their modeling.
the study of star formation in magnetized clouds, and in particular with the role played by magnetic fields in the process of star formation.

the observations of IRAS 2A and 4A are consistent with a magnetically dominated scenario for the formation and evolution of low-mass protoplanetary systems.

the magnetic field is dynamically important, but not dominant in this system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic field is a crucial factor in the process of cloud collapse and the formation of stars.
the observations and models are consistent with a magnetohydrodynamic collapse scenario.
the polarized emission observations toward IRAS 1333 4A are consistent with a magnetohydrodynamical collapse scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic field can be a key ingredient for the formation of protostars.
observations of polarized submillimeter emission can be used to discriminate among different collapse models.
the magnetic field is a key ingredient for the formation of stars, and it should be considered when modeling the collapse of clouds and the formation of protostars.
